articles.title: ‘I relive that mission every single day of my life’: how Black soldiers handled the Vietnam war
articles.summary: In ambitious documentary Soul Patrol, the complicated experiences of the Vietnam war’s first Black special ops team are explored both on and off the battleground. Ask the average American to name an elite US fighting force, and they might kick off with the Rangers or the Seals.
body: Known as long-range reconnaissance patrols, or LRRPs, these small teams of six to eight soldiers were dropped behind enemy lines to track supply routes and hostile positions, sometimes for days at a time. Stealth was essential. Their job was to identify targets and call in the cavalry, usually in the form of airstrikes, while avoiding direct engagement with enemy forces to preserve their cover.

A melancholy new documentary reckons with the weight of it all. Directed by Harper, Soul Patrol uncovers this hidden chapter of US military history: the story of army team 2/6 of company F, 51st infantry, the Vietnam war’s first Black special operations team – a ragtag bunch of daredevils and dreamers who snuck into the jungle, stared down death and lived to tell a tale that has taken half a century to share in living color. Based on a 2003 war memoir of the same name, the film follows author Ed Emanuel as he assembles the team for a gathering that edges from high school reunion to PTSD group therapy session.
The survivor’s guilt has haunted the team ever since. “I relive that mission every single day of my life,” Emanuel says. “We survived the war, but there was no peace.”

Ask the average American to name an elite US fighting force, and they might kick off with the Rangers or the Seals.

body: Paweł Pawlikowski ’s “ Fatherland,” which centers on the relationship between the writer Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika, leads the contest for the 39th European Film Awards, followed close behind by Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi’s “ La Bola Negra.”

The nominations, which were announced by the European Film Academy on Saturday at the Thessaloniki Film Festival in Greece, were based on the votes of the 5,700 members of the academy. The winners will be unveiled on Jan. 16 in Athens.
In third place was Cristian Mungiu’s Palme d’Or winner “Fjord” with five nominations, followed by Markus Schleinzer’s “Rose” with four nominations.
Pawlikowski, Calvo and Ambrossi, and Mungiu are competing for best director, alongside Sandra Wollner for “Everytime” and Andrey Zvyagintsev for “Minotaur,” winner of Cannes’ Grand Prix.

articles.title: Why so much love between Ireland and Garth Brooks?
articles.summary: Country music superstar Garth Brooks will perform a multi-city tour of Ireland in 2027.
body: Fans of Garth Brooks will be brushing off their Stetsons and polishing their cowboy boots after the country music superstar announced he will be performing in multiple cities across Ireland in 2027.
The tour includes Belfast, Galway, Kilkenny, Limerick and Cork and will be the first time he has played in Northern Ireland since his King's Hall gig in November 1998.

The singer has said in the past that Ireland is his favourite place in the world to sing, and the love appears to be mutual as his first two Belfast concerts sold out, with an extra date already added.
So why has an American country music star remained so popular with Irish fans for so many years?

articles.title: Michael Mann Seeks to Reclaim Rights to Original ‘Heat’ Screenplay
articles.summary: Michael Mann, who is set to begin shooting the long-awaited “Heat 2” in January, is in a legal dispute with New Regency as he seeks to reclaim the copyright to his screenplay for the original film. New Regency produced “Heat,” released in 1995.
body: New Regency argues that Mann’s termination action clouds its ownership of the original “Heat,” and is seeking a declaration that the termination notices are void.
Mann’s lawyers intend to fight the lawsuit “vigorously,” his reps said in a statement.

“We will vigorously defend this action and are confident that the courts will vindicate Michael Mann’s statutory rights under the Copyright Act,” a spokesperson said. “This filing has to do with original and personal writing Michael Mann did on multiple screenplays during the 1980s and which evolved into the iconic 1995 film ‘Heat’ that Mann wrote, produced and directed. After 40 years Michael Mann is exercising the right of authors to reclaim their work and in this case Michael Mann’s original creation.”

Mann developed the characters and the story that would become “Heat” over two decades, beginning in the 1970s. According to the lawsuit, Warner Bros. acquired the rights to the “Heat” screenplay in 1994 in a deal with Mann’s loan-out company. The suit alleges that deal was explicitly a “work made for hire” agreement — not an assignment of rights — and that therefore it cannot be terminated.

articles.title: ‘Fatherland,’ ‘La Bola Negra,’ ‘Fjord’ Lead European Film Award Nominations
articles.summary: Sandra Hüller scored a dual best actress nom for 'Fatherland' and 'Rose,' with Renate Reinsve, Sebastian Stan, Penelope Cruz, Javier Bardem and Andrew Scott among the acting nominees.
body: Pawel Pawlikowski’s German black-and-white period drama Fatherland, and La Bola Negra, a gay Spanish epic from director Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo, are the frontrunners for the 2027 European Film Awards, with Fatherland racking up 11 EFA nominations to 10 for La Bola Negra.

Hüller received a second best European actress nom, for her starring role as a 17th-century woman masquerading as a man in Markus Schleinzer’s Rose. She’s going up against Penélope Cruz, nominated for Florian Zeller’s Bunker; Léa Seydoux for her leading role in Marie Kreutzer’s Gentle Monster; Mathilde Arcel for her performance in May el-Toukhy’s Venice Festival winner Woman Unknown; and Renate Reinsve for her starring role in Cristian Mungiu’s Palme d’Or-winning Fjord.

articles.title: Even Grand Theft Auto's original creators haven't been able to play GTA 6
articles.summary: The next title in the series is expected to be the biggest video game release ever.
body: After a 13-year wait, two delays, and several high-profile leaks, the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 is fast approaching.
The next chapter in the nearly 30-year-old series, where players explore open worlds and break the law, has created an extraordinary level of anticipation.
And with developer Rockstar Games keeping their biggest release yet, tightly under wraps, even the people who helped bring the original to life aren't getting special treatment.
"We're all waiting to see what they've done," Dave Jones, GTA's co-creator, tells me, sitting alongside the original game's writer and publicist, Brian Baglow.

articles.title: Modern Fairy Tale ‘Mo Amor’ Explores Identity, Transformation and Love in All Its Forms
articles.summary: Estonian director Eeva Mägi is back at the Tallinn Black Nights Film Fest with her tender new film about a photographer, Princess Niina and her three suitors: The Mentor, The Writer and The Stonemason.
body: Mo Amor gets its world premiere on Monday, Nov. 16, in the Critics’ Picks Competition of the festival. Mägi’s previous film, Mo Papa, opened Tallinn’s Critics’ Picks section last year and earned a special mention.

Mägi wrote and directed the film and produced it with Sten-Johan Lill, who also handled the cinematography. The editor was Jette Keedus. The cast features Mo Papa stars Ester Kuntu and Jarmo Reha, one of this year’s 10 rising stars in Tallinn’s Black Nights Stars showcase, as well as Tambet Tuisk, Andres Mähar, Sander Roosimägi and Ivor Mikker.
Ahead of the film’s Tallinn world premiere, Mägi talked to THR about the inspiration for the film, how identity is used in political rhetoric and the lyrical quality of Mo Amor.
